channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Depois de cair no buraco, Flávio joga terra em cima de si mesmo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, after being involved in a controversial audio in which he asks Daniel Vorcaro for money, has adopted a self-destructive strategy, worsening his situation instead of correcting it. He continues to deepen his mistakes, like digging a bigger hole after falling into one. His conduct makes an already poor strategy even worse.

item.title: Lula x Flávio: o ponto central do novo Datafolha sobre a eleição de 2026
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll shows a technical tie in a hypothetical runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, both at 45%, while in the first round Lula leads narrowly at 38% to Flávio’s 35% — within the margin of error. Government approval remains low, with 51% disapproving and 39% rating it as bad or terrible, indicating a solid base but limited room for growth. Ciro Gomes’ entry at 5% slightly reduces the top two candidates’ shares but does not shift the core polarization.

item.title: Lula diz que relação pessoal com Trump pode evitar novas tarifas, em entrevista ao Washington Post
item.description: Lula stated that his positive personal relationship with Donald Trump could prevent new tariffs on Brazil and attract U.S. investments, despite political disagreements. He emphasized that the U.S. should treat Brazil with respect as a democratically elected leader and view Latin America as a partner, not a target for interference.

item.title: Onda de candidatos ligados ao 8 de Janeiro marca a corrida por vagas no Congresso
item.description: The suspension of the Dosimetry Law by Minister Alexandre de Moraes sparked protests from opposition lawmakers, who accuse the STF of overreaching legislative authority and threatening democracy. Three presidential pre-candidates — Flávio Bolsonaro, Ronaldo Caiado, and Romeu Zema — denounced the decision as an attack on the separation of powers. The legacy of January 8 and its judicial aftermath will remain central in the 2026 electoral campaigns.

item.title: Zema critica, Flávio Bolsonaro responde e fica tudo bem. Será?
item.description: Romeu Zema criticized Flávio Bolsonaro's audio asking for money from detained banker Daniel Vorcaro as 'imperdoável', prompting a restrained response from the senator, who called Zema 'precipitated' and 'new to politics'. Noblat's analysis suggests Flávio's moderate tone is a desperate attempt to pose as the moderate of the Bolsonaro clan to prevent the definitive rupture of the right-wing alliance for 2026, despite growing isolation and political damage from the Vorcaro scandal.

item.title: “Vaquinha”, candidaturas e votação: veja os próximo prazos eleitorais
item.description: With the deadline for voter registration regularization ending on May 6, Minas Gerais enters a new phase of the 2026 electoral calendar, launching the 'electoral vaquinha' on May 15, allowing pre-candidates to raise funds via crowdfunding without conducting early campaigning. On June 16, the TSE will disclose the Electoral Fund amount, and from June 30, radio and TV broadcasters will be prohibited from airing programs hosted by pre-candidates.

item.title: MG: com palanque de Lula indefinido, Cleitinho avança entre eleitores de esquerda
item.description: Senator Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos), a possible candidate for governor of Minas Gerais in 2026, is gaining support among left-leaning voters despite declaring support for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the presidential race. His social media popularity stems from simple communication, cross-ideological policies (such as reducing work hours and criticizing tolls), and frequent use of soccer jerseys, setting him apart from more religious allies like Nikolas Ferreira.

item.title: Aliados veem risco em aposta do governo Lula no fim da escala 6x1
item.description: The Lula government is betting on ending the 6x1 work schedule as its central electoral banner in Congress, backed by a heavy advertising campaign from Secom. Allies warn the move poses political risk due to sectoral resistance and fiscal pressures.

item.title: Para azar dos brasileiros, a lista de 'autoridades' ligadas a Vorcaro segue aumentando
item.description: The article claims that Daniel Vorcaro's influence network reveals connections with various Brazilian authorities, including Alexandre de Moraes, Ciro Nogueira, and Michel Temer, suggesting a lack of ethical conduct. Presented as exclusive content for subscribers, it calls for registration to access the full story. The tone is critical, implying a scandal involving corruption or influence peddling among political and judicial figures.

item.title: Garotinho envia a ministério denúncia contra pré-candidato ao Senado
item.description: Anthony Garotinho, pre-candidate for Rio de Janeiro governor from the Republicans party, filed a complaint with the Ministry of Justice against Márcio Canella, former mayor of Belford Roxo and Senate pre-candidate from União Brasil, accusing him of drug trafficking, militia ties, systemic corruption, and money laundering. The complaint includes allegations of threats against Garotinho’s family and requests for preventive detention and breaking of secrecy. These accusations had previously led to a court order in March requiring Garotinho to remove the posts or face daily fines.

item.title: Reação de Flávio Bolsonaro ao caso Vorcaro expõe diferença em relação ao método de Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro released a video admitting he solicited 'private sponsorship' from Daniel Vorcaro shortly after their intimate relationship was revealed, causing dissatisfaction within his circle. This approach contrasted with Lula's more restrained handling of similar situations, highlighting a methodological difference between the two figures.

item.title: Os repasses milionários do governo Lula à agência do chefe de comunicação de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The advertising agency Cálix Propaganda, linked to Marcello Lopes, communications coordinator for Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, received R$ 71.5 million from the Lula government for services provided to the Ministries of Transport and Regional Integration and Development. The revelation highlights a multi-million-dollar contract between a company tied to the opposition and the Workers' Party administration, raising concerns about potential conflicts of interest and misuse of public funds. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Lula na posse do novo ministro do TCU
item.description: President Lula plans to attend the swearing-in of former federal deputy Odair Cunha as the new minister of the Federal Court of Accounts (TCU), scheduled for next Wednesday (May 20) in Brasília. Cunha’s appointment was signed by Lula on April 28, and he was elected by the Chamber with 303 votes. Government ministers and Centrão parliamentarians are also expected to attend the ceremony.

item.title: Verdade ou mentira?
item.description: A Blog do Noblat poll shows that 97.8% of respondents believe Flávio Bolsonaro was caught in many lies, while only 2.2% think he told only the truth. Based on 139 responses, the survey reflects widespread public skepticism about the pre-candidate’s honesty.

item.title: Jogos de hoje, domingo, 17 de maio: onde assistir futebol ao vivo e horários
item.description: Sunday, May 17, 2026, features a packed football schedule with decisive matches across Europe and Brazil. In Europe, highlights include Premier League fixtures (Manchester United vs Nottingham Forest, Leeds vs Brighton, Everton vs Sunderland), La Liga (Sevilla vs Real Madrid, Barcelona vs Betis) and Serie A (Roma vs Lazio, Genoa vs Milan, Juventus vs Fiorentina). In Brazil, Série A matches include Santos vs Coritiba, Botafogo vs Corinthians, Bahia vs Grêmio and Athletico-PR vs Flamengo, broadcast on ESPN, Disney+, CazéTV and Xsports.

item.title: Flávio defendeu cloroquina e criticou medidas contra Covid, antes de ser pró-vacina
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) promoted the use of chloroquine and criticized Covid-19 containment measures during the early stages of the pandemic, opposing scientific consensus before later supporting vaccination. He cites this behavior as evidence of his 'moderation' compared to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, despite his initial stance contradicting expert opinion.

item.title: A esperança de Jorge Messias de ser indicado novamente para o STF
item.description: Jorge Messias, current head of the Advocacy-General of the Union (AGU), remains hopeful of being nominated again by Lula to the Supreme Federal Court (STF), despite his prior rejection by the Senate. Sources close to him say he remains confident in a future appointment, though the full article requires a subscription.

item.title: Alcolumbre se sente injustiçado por Lula no episódio de Messias
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre told allies he feels unjustly treated by the Lula government following the rejection of Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF, claiming he was the only one who warned in advance that Messias lacked sufficient votes. The nomination was defeated 42-34, despite government predictions of 45 favorable votes. Alcolumbre is alleged to have orchestrated the defeat with the opposition and had preferred Lula to nominate Rodrigo Pacheco to the Supreme Court.

item.title: Fim da taxa das blusinhas é primeira reação do governo às derrotas recentes no Congresso
item.description: The Lula government revoked the 'blusinhas tax' via Provisional Measure after internal polls showed 70% rejection of the 20% import tax on international purchases under US$50. The measure, valid for up to 120 days (renewable), was announced less than five months before the 2026 elections and comes as a reaction to recent congressional defeats, including the rejection of Jorge Messias for the STF and the overturning of the Dosimetry Law veto. Opposition and Centrão lawmakers view the move as electoral, pressuring Congress to vote on the MP in a joint committee, while the government denies controversy and claims the measure was correct and popular.

item.title: Sucessão travada, Master e Refit: PL acumula baques no Rio, berço do bolsonarismo e reduto do partido
item.description: The PL in Rio de Janeiro is facing multiple setbacks in the state succession process, including a federal police operation against former governor Cláudio Castro, the exposure of Flávio Bolsonaro’s conversations with Banco Master’s Daniel Vorcaro, and the inability of Douglas Ruas to assume interim governorship due to court rulings keeping Judge Ricardo Couto in office. The party’s succession plan — which envisioned Castro running for Senate and Ruas as interim governor — collapsed due to Castro’s ineligibility, STF injunctions, and PSD pressure from Eduardo Paes, leaving the state without clear political leadership.

item.title: Após crise com Vorcaro, Flávio busca empresários da Faria Lima para acalmar mercado e sustentar candidatura
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-SP) will travel to São Paulo for meetings with Faria Lima business leaders to calm financial market backlash following controversy over his negotiations with banker Daniel Vorcaro to fund the film 'Dark Horse'. The move aims to reinforce his image as the leading right-wing presidential candidate for 2026, promoting a liberal economic agenda of tax cuts and deregulation, while allies worry the 'Master' scandal and Vorcaro affair have damaged his electoral viability among investors and sectors of the right.

item.title: Aliados de Lula atuam para reaproximá-lo de Moraes após caso Master e derrota de Messias
item.description: Despite believing Alexandre de Moraes influenced the rejection of Jorge Messias to the STF, Lula's allies are working behind the scenes to bring the president and justice closer together. Distrust stems from Moraes' proximity to Senate President Davi Alcolumbre and alleged links to the Master case involving suspects tied to Daniel Vorcaro. However, PT officials believe a definitive rupture would be inconvenient for both sides, especially if Lula is re-elected and must coexist with Moraes as heads of power.

item.title: Juros escalam com candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro ameaçada pelo 'caso Dark Horse'
item.description: Brazilian government bond yields surged after messages emerged between pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and former Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro, raising concerns over the 'Dark Horse' case. The threat to Bolsonaro’s candidacy triggered market instability, reflecting investor worries about political risks and governability. This reaction underscores the financial market’s sensitivity to political figures linked to financial investigations.

item.title: Bondades eleitoreiras terão custo alto
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is implementing popular measures — such as fuel subsidies, expanded credit, and debt renegotiation — to boost his re-election bid in 2026, despite their high fiscal cost and negative impact on public debt. The latest initiative is a credit line to finance vehicles for app-based drivers and taxi operators, extending the electoral 'generosities' package. While politically appealing, these policies bypass fiscal targets and will burden public finances regardless of the election outcome.

item.title: Geração prateada tem peso na eleição
item.description: The Brazilian electorate aged 60 or older grew by 74% between 2010 and 2026, far exceeding the 15% increase in the total electorate during the same period, according to a Nexus study based on TSE data. This growth reflects a structural transformation in Brazilian democracy, with the voting power of older citizens gaining increasing influence in elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro apela à Bíblia e insiste que sonho presidencial não acabou
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro delivered a speech following the revelation of his business dealings with Daniel Vorcaro, citing the Bible, exalting his father’s figure, and insisting that the family’s presidential dream is not over. The event took place on Friday night, surrounded by allies, with a patriotic and religious tone, but no dance. The article is exclusive to subscribers and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Datafolha: 39% avaliam governo Lula como ruim ou péssimo; 30% como ótimo ou bom
item.description: According to a Datafolha poll released on May 16, 39% of voters evaluate Lula's government as bad or terrible, 30% as good or excellent, and 29% as regular, showing stability compared to April's survey. Lula's approval remains at 45%, with disapproval at 51%, unchanged from previous months. Furthermore, 59% of respondents believe Lula has delivered less than expected after three years and four months in office.

item.title: Fundo ligado a aliado de Eduardo compra casa no Texas
item.description: The Mercury Legacy Trust, a fund linked to Paulo Calixto — lawyer for Eduardo Bolsonaro in the U.S. — purchased a home in Arlington, Texas, for $753,500. The fund received $2 million from banker Daniel Vorcaro to finance the film 'Dark Horse,' a biopic about Jair Bolsonaro. The purchase, signed by André Porciúncula, former Bolsonaro government culture secretary, occurred in February and is tied to Eduardo Bolsonaro’s political activities in the U.S., now under investigation by the Federal Police.

item.title: Avaliação negativa do governo oscila para 39%, aponta Datafolha; 30% o consideram bom ou ótimo
item.description: Negative evaluation of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government dropped to 39%, according to a Datafolha poll, while 30% of respondents rated it as good or excellent. The share viewing the administration as poor or terrible decreased slightly compared to prior surveys, signaling a modest improvement in public perception. Nevertheless, a majority remains dissatisfied, reflecting ongoing polarization.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que não há nada errado com filme sobre Jair
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro defended the financing of the film 'Dark Horse', which portrays his father Jair Bolsonaro's trajectory, stating there is nothing wrong with the funding. He responded to criticism from his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro, who denied benefiting from the funds and labeled the accusations as false narratives. The case involves allegations of a US$24 million payment between Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro, founder of Banco Master, who is currently imprisoned in the Compliance Zero operation.

item.title: Após classificar como ‘imperdoável’ pedido de Flávio a Vorcaro, Zema minimiza: ‘Página virada’
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) called Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) request for money from banker Daniel Vorcaro 'imperdoável' but said the matter is 'a closed chapter,' emphasizing no rupture in the right-wing alliance and unity among conservative candidacies against the PT in the 2026 second round.

item.title: Governo Lula anuncia R$ 37 bi para o refino em São Paulo
item.description: The Lula government announced, through Petrobras, a R$ 37 billion investment plan for the state of São Paulo from 2026 to 2030, focusing on refining, bio-refining, exploration and production, gas, energy, biofuels, and logistics infrastructure. President Lula will attend an official visit to Replan on May 18, 2026, where the package will be unveiled, expected to generate 38,000 direct and indirect jobs. The refining segment will receive R$ 17 billion, with R$ 6 billion allocated exclusively to Replan, Petrobras' largest refinery.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro empatam em 45% no segundo turno, segundo pesquisa
item.description: A Datafolha poll released on Saturday (16) shows a technical tie between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in a simulated 2026 runoff, with both candidates at 45% of voting intentions. The result reflects a highly polarized electoral landscape in Brazil.

item.title: Leia a íntegra da nota do DC que lança Joaquim Barbosa ao Planalto
item.description: The Christian Democracy (DC) party officially launched Joaquim Barbosa, former president of the Supreme Federal Court (STF), as its pre-candidate for the 2026 Brazilian presidential election, replacing former minister Aldo Rebelo. The party’s statement emphasizes Barbosa as a unifying figure who can restore public trust in institutions and respond to society’s demand for change.

item.title: Datafolha: Avaliação negativa do governo Lula recua para 39%, e positiva oscila para 30%
item.description: Lula’s government negative approval dropped slightly from 40% to 39%, while positive approval rose from 29% to 30%, according to a Datafolha poll released Saturday. Among Lula voters, 68% rate his government as good or excellent, whereas 75% of Flávio Bolsonaro supporters view it negatively. The survey, conducted May 12–13 with 2,004 voters aged 16+, has a two-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Pré-candidatura de Joaquim Barbosa à Presidência já está posta, diz presidente do DC
item.description: The president of the Christian Democracy party (DC), João Caldas, confirmed that former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa is the party's pre-candidate for president in 2026, replacing Aldo Rebelo. The decision was announced in an interview with Broadcast.

item.title: A popularidade de Lula no Datafolha a menos de 5 meses da eleição
item.description: A Datafolha poll shows 30% of voters rate Lula's government as good or excellent, 39% as bad or terrible, and 29% as regular, indicating stability compared to April's round. The institute interviewed 2,004 voters between May 12 and 13, 2026, with a two-point margin of error and 95% confidence level. Negative evaluations are higher among men (41%) than women (37%).

item.title: Datafolha: 39% avaliam governo Lula como ruim ou péssimo e 30% aprovam petista
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll, released on May 16, shows that 39% of Brazilians rate President Lula's government as bad or terrible, while 30% approve and 29% consider it regular. These figures remain stable compared to the April survey, which showed 40% disapproval, 29% approval and 29% regular evaluation. The poll interviewed 2,004 people aged 16 or older between May 13 and 14, prior to the controversy involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro promete subir rampa do Planalto com condenados do 8/1
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) stated that if he wins the 2026 presidential election, he will bring those convicted of the January 8, 2023 attacks to walk up the ramp of the Planalto Palace in 2027. He described the defendants as victims of political persecution during a speech in Sorocaba, São Paulo. The remark reinforces a narrative of amnesty and reintegration for participants in the anti-democratic acts.

item.title: DC lança Joaquim Barbosa como pré-candidato à Presidência
item.description: The Christian Democracy party officially announced Joaquim Barbosa, former president of the Supreme Federal Court, as its pre-candidate for the 2026 Brazilian presidency, replacing Aldo Rebelo. The party states Barbosa embodies national unity and the restoration of public trust in institutions. Rebelo criticized the move as an 'affront' and vowed to remain in the race.

item.title: DC filia Joaquim Barbosa, fala em candidatura a presidente e abre crise com Aldo Rebelo
item.description: The Christian Democracy (DC) party affiliated former Supreme Court Justice Joaquim Barbosa and announced him as its pre-candidate for president, triggering an internal crisis with former Defense Minister Aldo Rebelo, who had been the party’s presumptive nominee. Party president João Caldas stated the change was made 'by the people' and that Rebelo failed to poll, while Rebelo rejected the move as a violation of transparency and democratic processes within the party.

item.title: TSE diz que teste confirma segurança das urnas
item.description: The TSE completed the second phase of the Public Security Test of Electronic Voting Machines, held from May 13 to 15, 2026, in Brasília, confirming the security of Brazil's electoral system. No findings compromised vote secrecy or integrity, and previous expert recommendations were incorporated. Final reports will be published on July 22, followed by the Digital Signature and Sealing Ceremony for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Indignação de Zema com Flávio era de vidro, e já se estilhaçou!
item.description: Romeu Zema expressed outrage for just 48 hours after condemning an audio in which Flávio Bolsonaro asked Daniel Vorcaro for money, calling it a 'slap in Brazil's face.' Yet, he quickly reconciled, offering 'the other cheek.' The reaction was brief and fleeting, highlighting the volatility of political alliances.

item.title: Datafolha: Governo Lula tem 39% de avaliação negativa e 30% de positiva
item.description: According to a Datafolha poll released on May 16, 2026, 39% of Brazilians evaluate President Lula's government as bad or terrible, compared to 30% who rate it as good or excellent and 29% who consider it regular. The negative assessment exceeds the positive by 9 percentage points, indicating wear and tear after three years and four months in office.

item.title: IA pode ampliar disseminação de fake news nas eleições
item.description: The use of artificial intelligence in the 2026 elections may amplify the spread of fake news, particularly amid political polarization and low digital literacy. Experts warn that electoral justice may lag behind evolving AI-driven manipulation tactics, akin to doping staying ahead of anti-doping efforts in sports. Minister Nunes Marques of the TSE prioritizes countering AI’s harmful effects, promoting debate and dialogue, and fostering unity among electoral courts to avoid either overly interventionist or overly liberal approaches.

item.title: José Dirceu reafirma apoio à reeleição de Lula
item.description: Former minister José Dirceu reaffirmed his support for Lula's re-election and stated he will focus his federal deputy candidacy on supporting Fernando Haddad for São Paulo governor and Simone Tebet for the Senate. He also emphasized the PT's goal of electing 15 federal deputies and avoiding a 'historical setback'.

item.title: Empate Lula-Flávio? Pesquisa Datafolha pré-“Dark Horse” já nasce morta
item.description: The Datafolha poll showing a 45%-45% tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro was deemed irrelevant because it was conducted mostly before the 'Dark Horse' scandal involving Flávio Bolsonaro and former banker Daniel Vorcaro was exposed. Since most interviews took place prior to the revelation, the data fails to capture the scandal's impact on voter intentions, rendering the poll useless for predicting post-controversy electoral dynamics.

item.title: Zema tem recorde de ‘curtidas’ ao criticar Flávio Bolsonaro, mas também ganha desafetos
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's presidential candidate, gained record social media engagement after criticizing Flávio Bolsonaro for allegedly negotiating with banker Daniel Vorcaro over sponsorships for a film about Jair Bolsonaro, calling the act 'unforgivable'. The video garnered over 4 million views, but drew internal criticism from Novo's Paraná directory, which called the move premature and misaligned with national party convention, while also ruling out a potential Flávio-Zema ticket.

item.title: Zema diz que crítica a Flávio por áudio com Vorcaro é ‘página virada’ e que não houve ruptura
item.description: Romeu Zema said his criticism of Flávio Bolsonaro for requesting money from Daniel Vorcaro was a 'closed chapter', denying any political rupture and stating they will unite in the second round against Lula. He said he acted according to his principles, but the alliance scenario remains unchanged.

item.title: Morre o locutor mineiro Milton Naves aos 67 anos
item.description: Milton Naves, a renowned Mineiro broadcaster, died at 67 in Belo Horizonte after over 50 years in radio, including 40 at Rádio Itatiaia and coverage of nine World Cups. His passing was mourned by former governor and presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema, who praised his lasting impact on Mineiro radio and sports culture.
